chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halbi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the properly slaughtered animal and the dead meat are mixed together, sell it to the one who considers the dead meat permissible (to eat), and eat its price.'

key_terms.الذَّكِيُّ: The properly slaughtered animal (according to Islamic rites)
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةُ: The dead meat (animal that died without ritual slaughter)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling mixed slaughtered and dead meat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi addresses the practical issue of disposing of mixed meat (khabith) by selling it to those who consider it permissible, such as Christians or Jews, thereby avoiding the waste of value while ensuring the seller does not consume the impurity itself. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the distinction between the impurity of the meat and the permissibility of its monetary value, allowing the seller to retain the price as clean wealth. This method of disposal is often preferred over burying or discarding the mixture to preserve economic utility.
